# Typed operations for the picks and the storyboard

<!-- Generated by `python -m bti.ops.doc` from the registry in bti/ops/. Do not edit this file: change the registry and run the command. -->

Every change to the picks (step 4, `picks.json`) and to the storyboard (step 5, `storyboard.json`) can be made with small
**named operations** instead of rewriting the whole file. Operations are sent in **batches**: the server checks the whole batch
before it writes anything, applies it all or not at all, records it in a change log, and can undo it. The page, an instruction
box, an agent in the app and an agent in a terminal use the same operations.

Every example below is written for the test fixture project (shots `s0001` to `s0010`, assets `A` to `D`, narration lines `b0001`
to `b0006`); it passes its own schema and applies to that project. `GET /api/ops/schema` gives the same schemas and examples as
JSON.

## Routes

| Method and path | What it does |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/projects/{pid}/picks/ops` | Apply a batch of picks operations. |
| `POST /api/projects/{pid}/storyboard/ops` | Apply a batch of storyboard operations. |
| `GET /api/projects/{pid}/changes?doc=picks\|storyboard&limit=50` | The change log, newest batch first, without the copies of the documents. `doc` is optional (both documents), `limit` is 1 to 200 (default 50). Answer: `{"changes": [record, ...]}`. |
| `POST /api/projects/{pid}/changes/{batch}/undo` | Undo one batch. Body: `{"base_rev", "actor", "note"?}`. Answer: like a batch, plus `undo_of`. |
| `GET /api/ops/schema` | `{"picks": {op: {summary, schema, example}}, "storyboard": {...}}`. |

## The batch request

```json
{
  "base_rev": "<the revision you read>",
  "actor": "agent:gemini-3.8-flash",
  "ops": [ {"op": "...", "...": "..."} ],
  "dry_run": false,
  "scope": null,
  "note": ""
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `base_rev` | The revision of the document you read (`rev` of `GET /api/projects/{pid}` for the storyboard, of `GET /api/projects/{pid}/picks` for the picks). A batch for any other revision is refused with `stale_revision` and nothing is written. |
| `actor` | Who sends it, one of: `human`, `agent:<model id>`, `cli:<name>`. Kept in the log; an item written by a batch gets `source: "human"` for `human`, `source: "agent"` for the others. |
| `ops` | 1 to 200 operations, applied in order. An operation sees what the earlier ones did. |
| `dry_run` | `true`: check everything and describe the changes, write nothing (the file on disk is byte-identical). An import is only checked for shape in a dry run, nothing is downloaded. |
| `scope` | `null`, or exactly one of `{"shots": [ids]}`, `{"chapters": [ids]}`, `{"beats": [ids]}`. An operation that touches anything outside it refuses the whole batch with `out_of_scope`. For the storyboard a shot is in a chapter or beat when it starts inside it; for the picks `beats` and `chapters` name narration lines, and operations that change something shared by every line (`set_main`, `set_region`, `remove_region`, an import with `as_main`) are outside any scope. A shot made by `split_shot` or `replace_range` from shots in scope is in scope. |
| `note` | Free text kept in the log, up to 2000 characters (for example the owner's request). |

Any other field is refused (`invalid_request`).

## The answer

```json
{
  "rev": "<revision after the batch>",
  "applied": 2,
  "batch": "batch_0007",
  "dry_run": false,
  "changes": [{"target": {"shot": "s0012"}, "time": "1:42", "what": "Cảnh 12: đổi kỹ thuật sang Zoom chậm"}],
  "issues": [],
  "created": {"shots": [], "overlays": [], "assets": [], "refs": {}}
}
```

- `batch` is the id in the change log; it is `null` for a dry run and for a batch that leaves the document as it was (nothing is written or logged then and `rev` is the revision it was). An operation that changed nothing when it ran has no entry in `changes`.
- `rev` is the revision after the write. For a dry run it is the current revision.
- `changes` has one entry per effect, in plain Vietnamese. `target` is `{"shot"}` (with `"overlay"` for an overlay), `{"beat"}` or `{"asset"}`; `time` is `m:ss` where the thing has a place in time, else `null`. In a dry run the asset of an import has no key yet: its target is `{"asset": null}`.
- `issues` are the validation issues of the resulting document (errors that were already there and warnings stay).
- `created` lists the ids the batch made: `shots`, `overlays` (`{shot, overlay}`), `assets`, and `refs` (name to id).

### Refs

An operation that creates something (`import`, `split_shot`, `add_overlay`, and a new shot of `replace_range`) can carry `"ref": "name"`. Any later field that names an asset, a shot or an overlay may then say `"$name"` instead of the id. Ids made by a batch are also deterministic: a new shot is `s` and one more than the largest shot number, padded to four digits; a new overlay is `o` and one more than the largest overlay number of the storyboard.

### All or nothing, and validation

If any operation is refused, nothing is written. After the operations, the document goes through the validation the existing save uses. An error that is **new** (not already in the document before the batch, found by its code and its place, by shot and overlay id) refuses the batch with `validation_failed`, with the issues and, for each, `op_index` of the operation that changed the shot it is about when that can be told. Problems that were already there before the batch never block it.

### Locks

A locked shot (or overlay) refuses every operation on it, whoever the actor is, except `unlock` (`locked`). `lock` on something already locked is refused too.

### What an approved document does when a batch changes it

A batch saves a document exactly as the page's own save does.

- **Storyboard** (`PUT /api/projects/{pid}/storyboard`): the `approvals` record is kept as it is; because the revision changed, the approval names an older revision and no longer stands, and the storyboard must be approved again. The previous file is copied to `history/`.
- **Picks** (`PUT /api/projects/{pid}/picks`): saving a document whose revision changed drops its approval, and the previous file is kept as `picks.prev.json`; the picks must be approved again. An undo that gives back exactly the content that was approved gives the approval back with it.

### The change log and undo

Every batch that wrote a document is one record in `projects/{pid}/changes/` (next to `history/`): `batch`, `doc`, `time`, `actor`, `note`, `ops` (as sent), `applied`, `changes`, `created`, `rev_before`, `rev_after`, `touched`, `undo_of`, `scope`, `copies`, and, in files of their own, the document before and after. The newest 200 records of each document are kept; only the newest 50 keep their copies (an older record is still listed, with `copies: false`, but cannot be undone: `undo_unavailable`). Pages' own saves (`PUT`) are not logged.

An undo puts back what the batch changed, and nothing else: each thing the batch changed (a shot; for the picks the main picture, a line, the regions of an asset, an asset) is compared with the batch's own copy of what it left. When all of them are still as the batch left them, each goes back to its value before the batch. When one was changed since, by a later batch or by a save of the page, nothing is undone: `undo_conflict` names the things and, when the log knows them, the later batches (`conflicts: [{thing, key, batches}]`). The newest batch of a document can be undone unless the page itself changed what it touched. An undo is a batch of the log (`undo_of`), so it can be undone.

A batch that is not made of typed operations and rewrites more than shots is a whole-document batch. Today that is `storyboard.retime` (its record names the operation `retime`): besides the shots it sets the end of the video and the `identity` of the storyboard (the style and the video's title). Its undo gives back everything it changed by the same rule: the shots, and each other part of the document (`end`, `identity`) that differs between the batch's two copies. A part that was changed since is a conflict like a shot, named `{"part": "end"}` (`key` `part:end`, no batches). The `changes` of such an undo have an entry `{"target": {"part": "end"}, "time": null, "what": ...}` for each part. Batches of typed operations are undone exactly as before.

## Errors

Every error body has `code`, `detail` (one English sentence), `fix` (one English imperative sentence an agent can act on) and `retry` (`no`, `after_fix` or `later`). When a field is wrong it has `fields: [{"path": "ops[1].params.region", "problem": "...", "allowed": [...]}]` (`allowed` whenever the set is small: region names, technique ids, slot names, enum values), and `op_index` names the operation. The `fix` below is the canonical sentence; a route may sharpen it for the case.

| Code | Status | Retry | Meaning | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `invalid_request` | 422 | `after_fix` | The request body is not valid for this route (a missing or wrong field of the envelope, a body that is not an object, a wrong number of operations, a bad scope). | Send a JSON body in the shape this route takes (the operation routes take base_rev, actor and 1 to 200 operations) and correct the fields listed. |
| `unknown_op` | 422 | `after_fix` | An operation name is not one of the operations of this document. | Use one of the operation names listed in allowed. |
| `invalid_field` | 422 | `after_fix` | A field of the request or of an operation is missing, has the wrong type, is out of range or is not allowed. | Correct the fields listed in `fields` and send the call again. |
| `unknown_shot` | 422 | `after_fix` | No shot with this id exists in the storyboard. | Use a shot id from allowed, or a $ref made by an earlier operation of the batch. |
| `unknown_overlay` | 422 | `after_fix` | The shot has no overlay with this id. | Use an overlay id of that shot from allowed, or a $ref made by an earlier operation. |
| `unknown_beat` | 422 | `after_fix` | No beat with this id exists in the narration. | Use a beat id of the approved narration (allowed lists them when there are few). |
| `unknown_asset` | 422 | `after_fix` | No asset with this key exists in the document. | Use an asset key from `allowed` (GET /api/projects/{pid}/picks lists the assets too), or import the picture first (an import operation and its $ref, or POST /api/projects/{pid}/picks/import). |
| `unknown_region` | 422 | `after_fix` | The asset has no region with this name. | Use one of the allowed region names, or add the region first with set_region. |
| `unknown_technique` | 422 | `after_fix` | No technique with this id exists in the style registry. | Use a technique id that exists (`allowed` lists them when there are few; GET /api/styles/{style} lists all of them). |
| `technique_not_offered` | 422 | `after_fix` | The technique exists but is hidden from a batch written by an agent: the program writes it, another technique replaces it, or it needs material the pictures step does not give. | Use the technique that `use` names instead (`allowed` lists the ones you are offered, `inputs/techniques.md` of a draft says when to use each). A batch of a person (the page, the actor `human`) may use any technique. |
| `wrong_technique_kind` | 422 | `after_fix` | The technique exists but its kind does not fit where it is used. | Use a technique of the kind that fits: base or card for a shot, overlay for an overlay. |
| `technique_unavailable` | 422 | `after_fix` | The technique is in the registry but the engine cannot draw it yet. | Use a technique the engine can draw (engine.available is true in the registry). |
| `unknown_param` | 422 | `after_fix` | The technique has no parameter with this name. | Use one of the allowed parameter names of this technique. |
| `unknown_slot` | 422 | `after_fix` | The technique has no slot with this name. | Use one of the allowed slot names of this technique. |
| `slot_kind_mismatch` | 422 | `after_fix` | The asset is of another kind than the slot takes (image, video or mask). | Use an asset of the kind the slot takes (allowed lists the kinds). |
| `unknown_ref` | 422 | `after_fix` | A $ref names nothing that an earlier operation of this batch created, or something of another kind. | Define the ref on an earlier operation of the batch (import, split_shot, add_overlay) before you use it. |
| `duplicate_ref` | 422 | `after_fix` | Two operations of the batch define the same ref. | Give every ref in a batch a different name. |
| `shot_too_short` | 422 | `after_fix` | The time would make a shot shorter than 0.2 seconds. | Choose a time that leaves every piece at least 0.2 seconds long. |
| `not_consecutive` | 422 | `after_fix` | The shots named are not a run of neighbours. | Give shots that follow each other in the storyboard, in their order. |
| `span_mismatch` | 422 | `after_fix` | The new shots of replace_range do not cover exactly the span of the shots they replace. | Make the first new shot start where the replaced run starts and keep every other start inside the run. |
| `video_not_main` | 422 | `after_fix` | A video cannot be the main picture. | Choose an image, not a video, as the main picture. |
| `locked` | 409 | `after_fix` | The shot (or overlay) is locked; every operation on it is refused except unlock. | Send unlock for that shot or overlay first, or leave it out of the batch. |
| `out_of_scope` | 422 | `after_fix` | An operation touches something outside the scope the batch declared. | Remove the operation from the batch, or send the batch with a wider scope. |
| `stale_revision` | 409 | `after_fix` | base_rev is not the current revision of the document; nothing was written. | Read the document again, apply your change to the revision in `current_rev`, then send the call again with base_rev set to it. |
| `validation_failed` | 422 | `after_fix` | The batch would leave the document with a new error that the existing save would refuse. | Correct every issue with level error in `issues` (the operations named by `op_index`, when there is one), then send again; nothing was written. |
| `undo_conflict` | 409 | `after_fix` | Something the batch changed was changed again since, so it cannot be put back. | Undo the later batches first (newest first), or leave the things named in conflicts as they are. |
| `undo_unavailable` | 409 | `no` | The record is still listed but its copies of the document are gone. | Make the change again with new operations: the copies of this batch were removed when the log was pruned. |
| `batch_not_found` | 404 | `no` | No batch with this id is in the log. | Take a batch id from the list at GET /api/projects/{pid}/changes. |
| `project_not_found` | 404 | `no` | No project with this id exists. | Take the project id from GET /api/projects. |
| `storyboard_not_found` | 404 | `after_fix` | The project has no storyboard yet. | Make the storyboard first: run the draft (POST /api/projects/{pid}/draft/start) and apply its proposal, then call again. |
| `document_corrupt` | 409 | `after_fix` | A file of the project cannot be read. | Restore a good copy of the file `detail` names (the storyboard has POST /api/projects/{pid}/storyboard/restore), then call again. |
| `unknown_source` | 422 | `after_fix` | The picture source of an import is not one of the known sources. | Use one of the picture sources commons, met, pexels, pixabay or osm (an import operation also takes book). |
| `not_found` | 404 | `after_fix` | What the call names does not exist (a picture that is not part of the project's books, a beat, an asset). | Use an id that exists: for a picture of the project's books take a source_id from GET /api/projects/{pid}/picks/book-images, for anything else list what exists with the matching GET route. |
| `source_rate_limited` | 503 | `later` | The picture source asked for fewer requests. | Wait `retry_after` seconds (a minute when it is null), then send the call again; nothing was written. |
| `source_unreachable` | 503 | `later` | The picture source is busy or did not answer. | Send the call again in a minute; nothing was written. |
| `source_error` | 502 | `after_fix` | The picture source answered with an error. | Choose another picture or another source, or try again in a minute; nothing was written. |
| `import_failed` | 502 | `no` | A picture could not be brought into the project (any other reason). | Check source and source_id, or choose another picture; nothing was written. |


## Picks operations

The document is `picks.json` (schema `bti.picks/1`): `main_asset`, `assets` (with `regions`), and per narration line `beats` with `items` (`asset`, `region`, `role`, `note`), `status` and `note`. A line with no pictures shows the main picture again.

### `set_main`

Choose the main picture (the whole painting) of the video.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `op` | `set_main` | yes | The operation name. |
| `asset` | text | yes | An asset key of the picks document (such as A12), or a $ref made by an import earlier in the batch. |

Example:

```json
{
  "op": "set_main",
  "asset": "B"
}
```

Sentence in `changes`: `Tranh chính: đổi sang {pic}`

### `set_region`

Set (add or replace) a named region of an asset: a point, with an optional radius, in pixels of the stored picture.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `op` | `set_region` | yes | The operation name. |
| `asset` | text | yes | An asset key of the picks document (such as A12), or a $ref made by an import earlier in the batch. |
| `region` | text | yes | A region name of the asset (letters, digits, spaces, _ . -). |
| `x` | number | yes | Centre, pixels from the left edge of the picture. |
| `y` | number | yes | Centre, pixels from the top edge of the picture. |
| `rx` | number | no | Horizontal radius in pixels; leave out for a point. |
| `ry` | number | no | Vertical radius in pixels; leave out for a point. |
| `label` | text | no | What the region shows, up to 80 characters. |
| `tight` | true or false | no | True when the region box was tightened by the second look and confirmed on a check picture. |
| `thing` | text | no | What the region shows, 2 to 8 English words (up to 120 characters). |
| `rough` | list of whole number | no | The rough box [x0, y0, x1, y1] in pixels of the stored picture before tightening (kept for the record). |

Example:

```json
{
  "op": "set_region",
  "asset": "A",
  "region": "MIRROR",
  "x": 700,
  "y": 420,
  "rx": 120,
  "ry": 120,
  "label": "The mirror",
  "tight": true,
  "thing": "convex mirror on back wall",
  "rough": [
    540,
    260,
    860,
    580
  ]
}
```

Sentence in `changes`: `Vùng {region} của {pic}: đã đặt`

### `remove_region`

Remove a named region of an asset (the pictures of a line that use it must be changed in the same batch, before this operation).

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `op` | `remove_region` | yes | The operation name. |
| `asset` | text | yes | An asset key of the picks document (such as A12), or a $ref made by an import earlier in the batch. |
| `region` | text | yes | A region name of the asset (letters, digits, spaces, _ . -). |

Example:

```json
{
  "op": "remove_region",
  "asset": "A",
  "region": "HANDS"
}
```

Sentence in `changes`: `Vùng {region} của {pic}: đã bỏ`

### `set_picks`

Replace all the pictures of one narration line (use skip_beat to show the main picture instead).

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `op` | `set_picks` | yes | The operation name. |
| `beat` | text | yes | A narration line (beat) id, such as b0003. |
| `items` | list of a picture item {asset, region?, role?, note?} | yes | The pictures of the line, in the order they are shown (1 to 30). |
| `reason` | text | no | Why these pictures; kept as the note of the line (up to 400 characters). |
| `kinds` | list of one of `detail`, `whole`, `outside`, `compare`, `journey`, `dates`, `figure`, `inscription`, `construction`, `relations`, `idea` | no | What the line does: one or two of detail, whole, outside, compare, journey, dates, figure, inscription, construction, relations, idea, in the order the line speaks (the automatic choice of pictures writes them). Leave it out to keep what the line has; send [] to remove it. |
| `missing` | list of a missing picture {what, code} | no | The pictures that were asked for the line and not found (at most 10). Leave it out to keep what the line has; send [] to remove it. |

Example:

```json
{
  "op": "set_picks",
  "beat": "b0003",
  "items": [
    {
      "asset": "B"
    },
    {
      "asset": "A",
      "region": "HEAD",
      "role": "detail"
    }
  ],
  "reason": "Both pictures show the room."
}
```

Sentence in `changes`: `Đoạn {n}: thay {k} hình`

### `add_pick`

Add one picture to a narration line, at the end or at a position.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `op` | `add_pick` | yes | The operation name. |
| `beat` | text | yes | A narration line (beat) id, such as b0003. |
| `asset` | text | yes | An asset key of the picks document (such as A12), or a $ref made by an import earlier in the batch. |
| `region` | text or null | no | A region of that asset to show, or null for the whole picture. |
| `role` | one of `main`, `detail`, `context`, `compare`, `document`, `map`, `video` | no | What the picture is for. |
| `note` | text | no | A short note (up to 400 characters). |
| `position` | whole number | no | Where to put it among the pictures of the line, counting from 0; leave out to add it last. |

Example:

```json
{
  "op": "add_pick",
  "beat": "b0004",
  "asset": "B",
  "role": "context"
}
```

Sentence in `changes`: `Đoạn {n}: thêm {pic}`

### `remove_pick`

Remove one picture of a narration line, by its position among the pictures of the line (counting from 0, as the earlier operations of the batch left them).

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `op` | `remove_pick` | yes | The operation name. |
| `beat` | text | yes | A narration line (beat) id, such as b0003. |
| `index` | whole number | yes | Position of the picture in the line, counting from 0. |

Example:

```json
{
  "op": "remove_pick",
  "beat": "b0001",
  "index": 0
}
```

Sentence in `changes`: `Đoạn {n}: bỏ {pic}`

### `skip_beat`

Make a narration line show the main picture again (it keeps no pictures of its own).

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `op` | `skip_beat` | yes | The operation name. |
| `beat` | text | yes | A narration line (beat) id, such as b0003. |
| `reason` | text | no | Why; kept as the note of the line (up to 400 characters). |
| `kinds` | list of one of `detail`, `whole`, `outside`, `compare`, `journey`, `dates`, `figure`, `inscription`, `construction`, `relations`, `idea` | no | What the line does: one or two of detail, whole, outside, compare, journey, dates, figure, inscription, construction, relations, idea, in the order the line speaks (the automatic choice of pictures writes them). Leave it out to keep what the line has; send [] to remove it. |
| `missing` | list of a missing picture {what, code} | no | The pictures that were asked for the line and not found (at most 10). Leave it out to keep what the line has; send [] to remove it. |

Example:

```json
{
  "op": "skip_beat",
  "beat": "b0003",
  "reason": "The main picture says it all."
}
```

Sentence in `changes`: `Đoạn {n}: dùng lại tranh chính`

### `import`

Bring one found picture into the project (the same sources and code path as POST .../picks/import and .../picks/import-book-image). Imports run first, before anything is written; a dry run only checks the shape. Videos are cut by the long job, not here. A download is polite and patient (one request a second to a host; a refusal of "too many requests" is waited for, up to about six minutes before the error `source_rate_limited`): send a batch with an import with a long timeout.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `op` | `import` | yes | The operation name. |
| `source` | one of `commons`, `met`, `pexels`, `pixabay`, `osm`, `web`, `book` | yes | Where the picture is found: a picture source, or `book` for a picture of the project's books. |
| `source_id` | text | yes | The id the search gave (or, for `book`, the source_id of GET .../picks/book-images). |
| `as_main` | true or false | no | Also make it the main picture. |
| `ref` | text | no | A name for the asset this operation brings in; later operations of the batch write it as $name. |

Example:

```json
{
  "op": "import",
  "source": "commons",
  "source_id": "File:Jan van Eyck - The Arnolfini Portrait - Google Art Project.jpg",
  "ref": "found"
}
```

Sentences in `changes`: `default` = `Nhập hình từ {source}`; `main` = `Nhập hình từ {source} và đặt làm tranh chính`

### `set_content_box`

Set the painted area of a picture: the box (pixels of the stored picture) that is the painting itself, without the black or grey ground of a museum photograph round a panel. The camera of the video never leaves the box of the main painting; the program finds one by itself when a picture is imported or made the main one, and this replaces what it found.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `op` | `set_content_box` | yes | The operation name. |
| `asset` | text | yes | An asset key of the picks document (such as A12), or a $ref made by an import earlier in the batch. |
| `x0` | number | yes | Left edge of the painted area, pixels from the left edge of the picture. |
| `y0` | number | yes | Top edge of the painted area, pixels from the top edge of the picture. |
| `x1` | number | yes | Right edge of the painted area, pixels from the left edge of the picture (more than x0). |
| `y1` | number | yes | Bottom edge of the painted area, pixels from the top edge of the picture (more than y0). |

Example:

```json
{
  "op": "set_content_box",
  "asset": "A",
  "x0": 40,
  "y0": 50,
  "x1": 1160,
  "y1": 1550
}
```

Sentence in `changes`: `Vùng tranh của {pic}: đã đặt`

### `clear_content_box`

Take away the painted area of a picture, so that the program finds it again from the picture (the main painting gets the new finding when the picks are saved).

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `op` | `clear_content_box` | yes | The operation name. |
| `asset` | text | yes | An asset key of the picks document (such as A12), or a $ref made by an import earlier in the batch. |

Example:

```json
{
  "op": "clear_content_box",
  "asset": "D"
}
```

Sentence in `changes`: `Vùng tranh của {pic}: để chương trình tự tìm lại`


## Storyboard operations

The document is `storyboard.json` (schema `bti.storyboard/1`). A shot lasts from its `start` to the `start` of the next shot (the last one to `end`); an anchor is `{"t": seconds}` or `{"w": word index, "off": seconds}`. A time given as a number of seconds is snapped to a word start within 0.35 s unless `snap` is false, as the page does.

### `set_technique`

Change the technique of a shot. Parameters not given take the defaults of the new technique (the same as POST .../defaults); slots that still fit are kept; the shot's note (the reason written for the old treatment) is cleared.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `op` | `set_technique` | yes | The operation name. |
| `shot` | text | yes | A shot id of the storyboard (such as s0012), or a $ref made by an earlier operation of the batch. |
| `technique` | text | yes | A technique id of the style registry, such as CAM-01 or HI-01. |
| `params` | object | no | Parameters of the new technique that differ from its defaults. |
| `intent` | one of `establish`, `explore`, `point_at`, `isolate`, `reveal`, `compare`, `context`, `quantify`, `explain_mechanism`, `quote`, `structure`, `transition` | no | What the shot or overlay is for. |

Example:

```json
{
  "op": "set_technique",
  "shot": "s0004",
  "technique": "CAM-03"
}
```

Sentence in `changes`: `Cảnh {n}: đổi kỹ thuật sang {technique}`

### `set_params`

Change some parameters of a shot or of one of its overlays. A value of null returns that parameter to its default.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `op` | `set_params` | yes | The operation name. |
| `shot` | text | yes | A shot id of the storyboard (such as s0012), or a $ref made by an earlier operation of the batch. |
| `overlay` | text | no | An overlay id of that shot (such as o2), or a $ref made by an earlier add_overlay. |
| `params` | object | yes | Parameters by name; a null value returns the parameter to its default. |

Example:

```json
{
  "op": "set_params",
  "shot": "s0002",
  "overlay": "o1",
  "params": {
    "rx": 260,
    "ry": 260
  }
}
```

Sentences in `changes`: `default` = `Cảnh {n}: đổi thiết lập {names}`; `overlay` = `Cảnh {n}: đổi thiết lập {names} của lớp phủ {technique}`

### `set_slot`

Put an asset into a slot of a shot or overlay (or empty the slot with asset null). When the main picture of a shot changes, its camera keys are fitted to the new picture the way the page does and its note (the reason written for the old picture) is cleared.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `op` | `set_slot` | yes | The operation name. |
| `shot` | text | yes | A shot id of the storyboard (such as s0012), or a $ref made by an earlier operation of the batch. |
| `overlay` | text | no | An overlay id of that shot (such as o2), or a $ref made by an earlier add_overlay. |
| `slot` | text | yes | A slot name of the technique, such as image. |
| `asset` | text or null | yes | An asset key of the storyboard, or null to empty the slot. |

Example:

```json
{
  "op": "set_slot",
  "shot": "s0004",
  "slot": "image",
  "asset": "C"
}
```

Sentences in `changes`: `default` = `Cảnh {n}: đổi ô {slot} sang {pic}`; `clear` = `Cảnh {n}: bỏ hình ở ô {slot}`; `overlay` = `Cảnh {n}: đổi ô {slot} của lớp phủ {technique} sang {pic}`; `overlay_clear` = `Cảnh {n}: bỏ hình ở ô {slot} của lớp phủ {technique}`

### `add_overlay`

Add an overlay (a ring of light, a label, an arrow...) to a shot. Parameters not given take the defaults of the technique; it starts at the start of the shot and, when dur and end are left out, HI-01 runs to the end of its shot while others last 3 s. A length past the end of the shot is cut to the shot.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `op` | `add_overlay` | yes | The operation name. |
| `shot` | text | yes | A shot id of the storyboard (such as s0012), or a $ref made by an earlier operation of the batch. |
| `ref` | text | no | A name for what this operation creates; later operations of the batch write it as $name. |
| `technique` | text | yes | A technique id of the style registry, such as CAM-01 or HI-01. |
| `start` | None or None | no | When the overlay starts; default: the start of the shot. |
| `dur` | number | no | How long it lasts, in seconds; cut to the end of the shot if longer. Leave out for HI-01 to run to the end of its shot (others default to 3 s). |
| `end` | None or None | no | When it ends (instead of dur); cut to the end of the shot if later. |
| `params` | object | no | Parameters by name; those not given take the defaults of the technique. |
| `slots` | object | no | Slots by name, `{slot: {"asset": key}}` (a text slot takes `{"text": ...}`). |
| `intent` | one of `establish`, `explore`, `point_at`, `isolate`, `reveal`, `compare`, `context`, `quantify`, `explain_mechanism`, `quote`, `structure`, `transition` | no | What the shot or overlay is for. |
| `note` | text | no | A short note (up to 400 characters). |

Example:

```json
{
  "op": "add_overlay",
  "shot": "s0004",
  "technique": "HI-01",
  "params": {
    "at": "CENTRE",
    "rx": 220,
    "ry": 220
  },
  "start": {
    "w": 70
  },
  "dur": 4,
  "ref": "ring"
}
```

Sentences in `changes`: `default` = `Cảnh {n}: thêm lớp phủ {technique}`; `region` = `Cảnh {n}: thêm lớp phủ {technique} ở vùng {region}`; `default_cut` = `Cảnh {n}: thêm lớp phủ {technique} (cắt đến hết cảnh)`; `region_cut` = `Cảnh {n}: thêm lớp phủ {technique} ở vùng {region} (cắt đến hết cảnh)`

### `set_overlay`

Change an overlay of a shot: its technique (parameters then take the new defaults), start, duration or end (cut to the shot if past its end), intent or note. Use set_params for its parameters.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `op` | `set_overlay` | yes | The operation name. |
| `shot` | text | yes | A shot id of the storyboard (such as s0012), or a $ref made by an earlier operation of the batch. |
| `overlay` | text | yes | An overlay id of that shot (such as o2), or a $ref made by an earlier add_overlay. |
| `technique` | text | no | A technique id of the style registry, such as CAM-01 or HI-01. |
| `start` | None or None | no | When the overlay starts; default: the start of the shot. |
| `dur` | number or null | no | Duration in seconds (cut to the shot if longer), or null to run to the end of the shot. |
| `end` | None or None or null | no | When it ends (instead of dur); null removes it. |
| `intent` | one of `establish`, `explore`, `point_at`, `isolate`, `reveal`, `compare`, `context`, `quantify`, `explain_mechanism`, `quote`, `structure`, `transition` | no | What the shot or overlay is for. |
| `note` | text | no | A short note (up to 400 characters). |

Example:

```json
{
  "op": "set_overlay",
  "shot": "s0002",
  "overlay": "o1",
  "dur": 3.5
}
```

Sentences in `changes`: `default` = `Cảnh {n}: sửa lớp phủ {technique}`; `cut` = `Cảnh {n}: sửa lớp phủ {technique} (cắt đến hết cảnh)`

### `remove_overlay`

Remove an overlay from a shot.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `op` | `remove_overlay` | yes | The operation name. |
| `shot` | text | yes | A shot id of the storyboard (such as s0012), or a $ref made by an earlier operation of the batch. |
| `overlay` | text | yes | An overlay id of that shot (such as o2), or a $ref made by an earlier add_overlay. |

Example:

```json
{
  "op": "remove_overlay",
  "shot": "s0002",
  "overlay": "o2"
}
```

Sentence in `changes`: `Cảnh {n}: bỏ lớp phủ {technique}`

### `split_shot`

Cut a shot in two at a time. Each half keeps the camera pose it had at that time and the overlays go to the half they start in (an overlay that crosses the cut is shortened), as when the page cuts.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `op` | `split_shot` | yes | The operation name. |
| `shot` | text | yes | A shot id of the storyboard (such as s0012), or a $ref made by an earlier operation of the batch. |
| `at` | number or None or None | yes | A time: a number of seconds (snapped to a word start within 0.35 s unless snap is false) or an anchor object. |
| `snap` | true or false | no | Snap a time given in seconds to the nearest word start within 0.35 s (default true); false keeps the exact time. |
| `ref` | text | no | A name for what this operation creates; later operations of the batch write it as $name. |

Example:

```json
{
  "op": "split_shot",
  "shot": "s0004",
  "at": 26.0,
  "ref": "second_half"
}
```

Sentence in `changes`: `Cảnh {n}: tách thành hai cảnh tại {at}`

### `merge_shots`

Merge shots that follow each other into the first of them: it keeps its camera poses over the time it had, takes the overlays of the others and lasts until the end of the last.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `op` | `merge_shots` | yes | The operation name. |
| `shots` | list of text | yes | The shot ids, in the order they follow each other in the storyboard (2 to 20); the first one remains. |

Example:

```json
{
  "op": "merge_shots",
  "shots": [
    "s0007",
    "s0008"
  ]
}
```

Sentence in `changes`: `Cảnh {n}: gộp với cảnh {others}`

### `move_boundary`

Move the cut where a shot begins to another time: the shot before it gets longer or shorter by the same amount. Overlays that no longer fit their shot are shifted or shortened, as when the page moves a cut.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `op` | `move_boundary` | yes | The operation name. |
| `shot` | text | yes | The shot that begins at the boundary to move (not the first shot of the storyboard). |
| `to` | number or None or None | yes | A time: a number of seconds (snapped to a word start within 0.35 s unless snap is false) or an anchor object. |
| `snap` | true or false | no | Snap a time given in seconds to the nearest word start within 0.35 s (default true); false keeps the exact time. |

Example:

```json
{
  "op": "move_boundary",
  "shot": "s0004",
  "to": 20.0
}
```

Sentence in `changes`: `Cảnh {n}: dời điểm cắt từ {old} sang {new}`

### `replace_range`

Replace a run of consecutive shots by new shots that cover exactly the same span of narration (the shape the fast edit produces: shots changed or added, others removed). The first new shot starts where the run starts; the others start inside it.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `op` | `replace_range` | yes | The operation name. |
| `from_shot` | text | yes | The first shot of the run. |
| `to_shot` | text | yes | The last shot of the run (the same shot for a run of one). |
| `shots` | list of a new shot | yes | The new shots, in time order (1 to 60). |

Example:

```json
{
  "op": "replace_range",
  "from_shot": "s0007",
  "to_shot": "s0008",
  "shots": [
    {
      "technique": "CAM-01",
      "intent": "explore",
      "slots": {
        "image": {
          "asset": "C"
        }
      },
      "ref": "first"
    },
    {
      "technique": "STATIC-01",
      "start": {
        "w": 154
      },
      "slots": {
        "image": {
          "asset": "B"
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Sentences in `changes`: `default` = `Cảnh {rng}: thay bằng {k} cảnh mới`; `cut` = `Cảnh {rng}: thay bằng {k} cảnh mới (lớp phủ cắt đến hết cảnh)`

### `lock`

Lock a shot (or one overlay of it): every operation on it is refused until it is unlocked, whoever sends it.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `op` | `lock` | yes | The operation name. |
| `shot` | text | yes | A shot id of the storyboard (such as s0012), or a $ref made by an earlier operation of the batch. |
| `overlay` | text | no | An overlay id of that shot (such as o2), or a $ref made by an earlier add_overlay. |

Example:

```json
{
  "op": "lock",
  "shot": "s0003"
}
```

Sentences in `changes`: `default` = `Cảnh {n}: đã khóa`; `overlay` = `Cảnh {n}: đã khóa lớp phủ {technique}`

### `unlock`

Unlock a shot (or one overlay of it). The only operation a locked shot accepts; unlocking something that is not locked changes nothing.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `op` | `unlock` | yes | The operation name. |
| `shot` | text | yes | A shot id of the storyboard (such as s0012), or a $ref made by an earlier operation of the batch. |
| `overlay` | text | no | An overlay id of that shot (such as o2), or a $ref made by an earlier add_overlay. |

Example:

```json
{
  "op": "unlock",
  "shot": "s0006"
}
```

Sentences in `changes`: `default` = `Cảnh {n}: đã mở khóa`; `overlay` = `Cảnh {n}: đã mở khóa lớp phủ {technique}`


## Sentences of an undo

An undo describes what it put back with these sentences (`changes` of the undo batch):

- storyboard: `restore`: Cảnh {n}: trở lại như trước khi sửa; `remove_added`: Đã bỏ cảnh {id} do lô được hoàn tác tạo ra; `restore_removed`: Cảnh {n}: đã khôi phục
- picks: `main`: Tranh chính: trở lại như trước, {pic}; `beat`: Đoạn {n}: trở lại như trước khi sửa; `regions`: Vùng của {pic}: trở lại như trước khi sửa; `asset_removed`: Đã bỏ {pic} khỏi dự án (do lô được hoàn tác nhập); `asset_restored`: Đã trả lại {pic} vào dự án
